proof_review: The general rank-three proof treats the four-group intersection separately: its two normal commuting dihedral factors have cyclic characteristic derived subgroups, which must be trivial. Independence and the endpoint four-group intersections supply all remaining subset intersections.

The acquired contraction criterion is applied only at pure adjacent edges of order three. Alternating path labels give the first product cycle and the second product of a 3-cycle and a disjoint transposition. The simplex endpoint has type 3^(n-2), not the printed type containing 6.

The deleted permutation module of S4 is faithful over F2 and F5. In characteristic five a vector minus its transposition produces a root vector; its orbit spans the module over any extension. Absolute irreducibility therefore does not repair the impossible Omega_3(5) lower containment.

Only the acquired projective form-preservation theorem is used for the PSL3/PGL3 exclusion. Classical group orders and natural irreducibility remain expressly borrowed; no arbitrary projective quotient is assumed to preserve IP.
